summary: 78-year-old woman with AF on warfarin (INR 4.8) and melaena; HR 108, SBP 104, Hb 9.4, urea 11.8 (GBS 13). Anticoagulant must be flagged for a clinician decision; no peri-operative LMWH bridging during an active bleed.

inputs.hpi: Two days of black tarry stools. Dizzy on standing this morning. Atrial fibrillation on warfarin; recently finished a course of clarithromycin for a chest infection. No haematemesis.

exam.abdomen: Soft, mildly tender epigastrium. PR: melaena.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Acute upper GI bleed on warfarin
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Acute upper GI bleed (melaena) on warfarin, INR 4.8, Glasgow-Blatchford 13. Anticoagulation management — clinician decision.

mustInclude.note: ESGE: withhold the VKA; give vitamin K and PCC if haemodynamically unstable. The choice is the clinician's.

mustExclude.note: An elective peri-operative bridging template (heparin) during active GI haemorrhage is contraindicated.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: computeClinicalPrompts anticoag_check (any anticoagulant) adds the elective peri-operative plan line "hold DOAC 48–72h pre-op; warfarin — bridge with LMWH per haematology protocol" to an actively bleeding patient.
mustExclude.proposedFix: clinical-inference.ts anticoag_check: suppress the bridging template when GI haemorrhage is present (gi_bleed_panel fired) and replace it with "Anticoagulant: withhold/reversal decision by clinician (ESGE 2021)".

mustExclude.note: Patient-directed hold/stop instructions are forbidden (hazard H-10).

mustExclude.knownGapNote: upper_gi_bleed protocol medications list "Tranexamic acid 1 g IV stat — if endoscopy is delayed and haemorrhage is trauma-related or massive"; it appears in every plan built on that protocol.
mustExclude.proposedFix: Remove tranexamic acid from the upper_gi_bleed protocol medications (ESGE 2021 recommends against it; HALT-IT). Surgeon sign-off needed.

guideline.name: ESGE Guideline — endoscopic diagnosis and management of nonvariceal upper gastrointestinal haemorrhage (NVUGIH), update 2021
guideline.section: Vitamin K antagonists: withhold; in haemodynamic instability give IV vitamin K and 4-factor PCC (FFP if unavailable); endoscopy not delayed for INR correction; tranexamic acid not recommended
guideline.citation: Gralnek IM, Stanley AJ, Morris AJ, et al. Endoscopy. 2021;53:300–332.

guideline.name: BSG-led multisociety consensus care bundle — early clinical management of acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding
guideline.section: Care bundle: identify and manage anticoagulants early; group and save
guideline.citation: Siau K, Hearnshaw S, Stanley AJ, et al. Frontline Gastroenterol. 2020;11:311–323.

guideline.name: NICE CG141 — Acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding in over 16s: management
guideline.section: Endoscopy within 24 h; treat patients on warfarin with PCC and vitamin K when actively bleeding
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Clinical guideline CG141. London: NICE; 2012 (last updated 2016).

guideline.name: HALT-IT randomised trial — tranexamic acid in gastrointestinal bleeding
guideline.section: Tranexamic acid: no benefit, more venous thromboembolism
guideline.citation: HALT-IT Trial Collaborators. Effects of a high-dose 24-h infusion of tranexamic acid on death and thromboembolic events in patients with acute gastrointestinal bleeding (HALT-IT). Lancet. 2020;395:1927–1936.

rationale: Permutation: anticoagulated elderly woman with a supratherapeutic INR (likely clarithromycin interaction). The engines must flag the anticoagulant and coagulopathy for a clinician decision and must not produce a peri-operative LMWH bridging plan or patient-directed stop/hold advice.

authoring.author: Claude (upper-GI cluster)
authoring.notes: Expectations need surgeon sign-off (reviewedBy). Citations written from the guideline texts, not yet checked against the source (verified: false).
